insight.title: Your Camera Is Guessing What You See
insight.subtitle: Why modern photography is a mathematical reconstruction rather than a capture of light.

sections.text: Your phone camera doesn't actually see what is in front of it. It ignores millions of light particles it deems "noise" and replaces them with what it predicts a perfect image should look like.

Tiny smartphone sensors cannot physically capture the detail we see on screens. To fix this, software "paints" over the image, using mathematical patterns to sharpen edges and generate colors that weren't actually there.
This is why modern photos often feel better than reality. The device isn't recording a memory; it is performing a high-speed reconstruction based on what it thinks you want to see.
A digital photo is a math equation, not a memory.
